newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Horse racing-Papillon favourite for Irish National.
newsitem.headline: Horse racing-Papillon favourite for Irish National.

text.p: Ted Walsh-trained Papillon has been backed down to 6-1 favourite from 10-1 last weekend for Monday's Grade One Irish Grand National at Fairyhouse.
British-trained raiders Mary Reveley's Seven Towers and David Nicholson's Percy Smollet are quoted 8-1 for the 100,000 Irish pound presentation at the County Meath racecourse.
Two other British-trained entries, Gordon Richards-trained The Grey Monk and Jenny Pitman's Mudahim, are quoted 10-1.
Walsh, who is based in County Kildare, has offered the ride on his novice over the three miles and five furlongs (4.7-km) trip to Ireland's champion jumps jockey Charlie Swan.
Swan is expected to make up his mind later this week.
Herring Gull, Vulpine, Bit Of A Skite and Vanton were all novices when they won the Irish National.
Walsh landed the biggest win of his training career when he saddled Commanche Court to win the Triumph Hurdle at the 1997 Cheltenham festival of racing.
